# Codegen

`@softistx/limix-codegen` turns two inputs into one TypeScript file that
registers them in `@softistx/limix`: the REST operations (an OpenAPI document)
and the GraphQL operations (SDL files or the schema graphql-codegen holds).
Core's `Register` interface reads the file by module augmentation, so
`definePolicy` checks against it. Codegen's only job is those types: it never
reads a policy, a YAML or JSON rules file included.

Writing the policy once the file exists: [Writing rules](writing-rules.md).

## The generated file

`generate` writes `src/generated/limix.ts`; `--out <file>` writes another path (never one of the inputs).

```ts
// Generated by @softistx/limix-codegen from schema.graphql, openapi.yaml.
// Do not edit: run `limix-codegen generate` again (`--check` in CI).

import type {
	ConditionName,
	GraphqlRulesInput,
	Register,
	RestRulesInput,
} from '@softistx/limix';

export type LimixRest = 'GET /notes' | 'GET /notes/:id' | 'DELETE /notes/:id';
export type RestRules<W extends string = ConditionName> = RestRulesInput<
	Register,
	W
>;
export type LimixGraphql = 'Mutation.createNote' | 'Note.body' | 'Query.me';
export type GraphqlRules<W extends string = ConditionName> = GraphqlRulesInput<
	Register,
	W
>;

declare module '@softistx/limix' {
	interface Register {
		rest: LimixRest;
		graphql: LimixGraphql;
	}
}
```

`RestRules` and `GraphqlRules` are written only when REST or GraphQL operations
are generated. They are the types of a block of rules kept in its own file:
`satisfies RestRules<'ownsBook'>` checks it against the API's operations and the
declared role and permission names, `'ownsBook'` being the condition names `when`
may use (`RestRules` alone accepts any declared condition name). See
[Splitting the policy across files](writing-rules.md#7-splitting-the-policy-across-files).
The import makes the file a module, which an augmentation needs anyway. With
several generated files, import `RestRules` from the one you mean: a barrel that
does `export *` over two of them makes the name ambiguous.

Commit it, and keep it inside your tsconfig `include`: the augmentation works
only when the file is in the program. The output is sorted (REST by path, then
method; the rest by code unit), LF, with a fixed header, so the same inputs
always give the same bytes. The header names the inputs relative to the working
directory, with `/`, sorted and each once, so flag order and absolute paths do
not change it. The plugin's second header line reads "run graphql-codegen
again". `--check` is "the file is missing or out of date", nothing more.

## What each key checks

| Key | Source | What it checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rest` | `--openapi` | `definePolicy`: a path key must be a path of the API, and a method under it a method the API declares on that path (or `*`); a flat key (`'GET /notes'`) must be an operation of the API |
| `graphql` | `--graphql` or the plugin | `definePolicy`: a type and a field must exist in the schema, on every type (roots and others), or the field `*`; a flat key (`'Query.me'`) must be a field, `'Note.*'` needs a type of the schema |

The role, permission and condition names are not generated, because that would
need codegen to read the policy. Declare them by hand; `definePolicy` then
narrows `roles`, `permissions` and `when` to them. See
[Declare the vocabulary](writing-rules.md#2-declare-the-vocabulary).

## What stays unchecked

- A key whose input was not given: without `--graphql`, GraphQL rules accept any
  type and field.
- A path key holding `*` or `{`: `/files/*path`, `/a{/:b}`, `'* /notes'` and
  `'/x/*'` name several routes and are accepted with any method. The types do not
  look at them. Coverage (`@softistx/limix/coverage`) reports a rule that reaches
  no operation of the spec, which is how a typo behind a wildcard or in a rules
  file is caught.
- Anything but an inline object literal given to `definePolicy`: a variable, a
  spread, an escaped `\*` key or a `{` key is accepted unchecked. Its result, a
  `Rules`, goes to `compilePolicy` directly.
- A rules file (YAML or JSON): it never goes through `definePolicy`, so the types
  do not see it. Check it against the API with `@softistx/limix/coverage`.
- A literal typed `as const`: the lists of `roles` and `permissions` are mutable
  in the types, so a readonly one is refused once names are declared.
- `HEAD` is registered only when the spec declares it.

## OpenAPI conversion

Keys are written without `global.basePath`; `servers` and Swagger 2 `basePath`
are ignored. Both OpenAPI 3.x and Swagger 2.0 are read, from `.yaml`, `.yml` or
`.json`. A path item that is a `$ref` is refused: bundle the spec first.

| OpenAPI | Rules file |
| --- | --- |
| `/notes/{id}` | `/notes/:id` |
| `/files/{id}.json` | `/files/:id.json` |
| `/files/{id}x` | `/files/:"id"x` (the name would run into the text) |
| `/files/{file-id}` | `/files/:"file-id"` (not an identifier) |
| `/a(b)` | `/a\(b\)` |
| `/a:b*` | `/a\:b\*` |

The path conversion is `rulesPathOf` from `@softistx/limix/coverage`, the same
function coverage uses, so the two cannot disagree on a path. A path it cannot
spell (an unbalanced brace, two adjacent parameters) is refused with the source's
name in front.

Each of `get put post delete options head patch trace query` under a path item
becomes an operation. `parameters`, `summary`, `description`, `servers`, `x-*`,
`additionalOperations` and `webhooks` are ignored.

## A starter policy

```sh
limix-codegen init --openapi openapi.yaml --graphql schema.graphql
```

writes `src/policy.ts` (`--out` picks another `.ts` file, `--types` says where
the generated file is so the import is right): a `definePolicy` call in which
every REST operation and every GraphQL root field gets `authenticated: true`
under `unmatched: 'deny'`. Only root fields are listed. `--flat` writes one key
per operation instead of a path or a type that holds its methods or fields:

```ts
import './generated/limix';
import { definePolicy } from '@softistx/limix';

export const rules = definePolicy({
	limix: 1,
	global: { unmatched: 'deny' },
	rest: {
		'GET /notes': { authenticated: true },
		'DELETE /notes/:id': { authenticated: true },
	},
	graphql: {
		'Query.me': { authenticated: true },
	},
});
```

From code, `starterPolicy(operations, { flat: true, types: './generated/limix' })`
returns the same text.

The two forms make the same policy; flat reads better once a file grows and
diffs by operation. The policy is built, run through `definePolicy` and
compiled before it is written. `init` never rewrites an existing file (it exits
0 with a notice), so follow up with coverage, which lists what is new:

```ts
import { coverage } from '@softistx/limix/coverage'
import { openapiOperations } from '@softistx/limix-codegen'
import { graphqlOperations } from '@softistx/limix-graxia/operations'

coverage(policy, [...openapiOperations(doc), ...graphqlOperations(sdl)])
```

## The graphql-codegen plugin

```ts
export default {
  schema: 'schema.graphql',
  generates: {
    'src/generated/limix.ts': {
      plugins: ['@softistx/limix-codegen/graphql-codegen'],
      config: { openapi: 'openapi.yaml' },
    },
  },
}
```

`openapi` is one file or a list; other keys (graphql-codegen merges its own, such
as `emitLegacyCommonJSImports`) are ignored, and 0.4 has no `rules` option. The
plugin needs no `@graphql-codegen/plugin-helpers`. It reads the OpenAPI files
through Bun, so start it with `bun --bun graphql-codegen` when you give one. It
relies on the one copy of `graphql` that graphql-codegen uses: with two copies it
stops with `two copies of graphql`, and you dedupe `graphql` in the lockfile. It
writes its own output file: GraphQL comes from the schema, so the header names
`the GraphQL schema`. graphql-codegen's own `--check` compares that file the way
it compares any other.

## Upgrading from 0.3

0.4 is types only. What went:

- `--rules` of `generate` and `init`, and the plugin's `rules` option: pass no
  rules file. A call that still names it fails (`Unknown option '--rules'`, exit
  2).
- The stale-rule report, and the `LimixPermission`, `LimixRole` and
  `LimixCondition` types with their `Register` keys. `--check` now means "the
  file is missing or out of date".
- The rules-file `init` (`--rules`, YAML or JSON, `starterRules`): `init` writes
  a TypeScript `policy.ts` (`--out`, default `src/policy.ts`; `starterPolicy`).

To move over:

1. Drop `--rules ...` from the scripts, and regenerate: `limix-codegen generate
   ...`. Regenerate **before** adding the hand declaration below, or the old
   generated `role` key and yours both declare it and TypeScript reports
   `Subsequent property declarations must have the same type` (see
   [troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md)).
2. Move the role, permission and condition names into a `declare module` block
   you write (see [Declare the vocabulary](writing-rules.md#2-declare-the-vocabulary)).
3. Write the policy in code with `definePolicy`, typed by the generated file.
   A YAML or JSON rules file still loads with `loadRules`, but codegen does not
   type it: check it against the API with `@softistx/limix/coverage`.
